server.description: macOS audio as live resources: output/input volume, mute and device switching.

io.github.maxf98.streamdeck-mcp/studio.longDescription: Exposes macOS audio as live MCP resources that push on change: output volume/mute (resource://audio/output), input (mic) volume/mute (resource://audio/input), and the device inventory with each device's live volume/mute + current defaults (resource://audio/devices). server.name: io.github.maxf98/clipboard
server.title: Clipboard
server.description: Read, write and transform the macOS clipboard. No permissions needed.

io.github.maxf98.streamdeck-mcp/studio.longDescription: Copy and paste programmatically: read, write, transform, and manage the macOS system clipboard. Supports plain text, HTML, RTF, images, file paths, and clipboard history. Needs no macOS permissions — the pasteboard isn't TCC-gated, so every tool works with no prompt. Reading the frontmost app's selection is not included: that requires synthesizing ⌘C, which needs Accessibility. Have the user copy first, then call get_clipboard.

server.name: io.github.maxf98/filesystem
server.title: Filesystem
server.description: Read, write, edit, move and search files within folders you explicitly allow.

io.github.maxf98.streamdeck-mcp/studio.longDescription: Read, write, edit, move and search files and directories on disk. Wraps the official @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem — every operation is confined to the folders you allow, and paths outside them are refused. Set the allowed roots in this pack's config before use.

roots.description: Folders the buttons may read and write. Everything outside them is refused — list specific project or documents folders, NOT / or your home directory.

server.name: io.github.maxf98/git
server.title: Git
server.description: Live repo status as a subscribable resource, plus commit, push, pull and stash.

io.github.maxf98.streamdeck-mcp/studio.longDescription: Repository state for buttons: branch, ahead/behind, and staged/unstaged/untracked counts as structured fields rather than porcelain a face would have to parse, plus commit, push, pull, fetch, branch switching and stashing. The point is resource://git/status/{repo} — a live, subscribable status that pushes when you save a file, commit or switch branches, so a key can show "main ↑1 ~3" without polling. Watching only runs while something is bound. No force-push, reset, rebase or amend: use the bash pack if you mean it.

default_repo.description: Absolute path to the repository buttons should act on when they don't name one. Lets a face be authored without hard-coding a path.

auto_fetch_seconds.description: How often to `git fetch` in the background while a face is bound, so ahead/behind stay true. Off by default (0) — a silent fetch on someone's repo should be asked for. 300 is a reasonable value.

poll_seconds.description: How often to re-read `git status` while a face is bound, which is how working-tree edits are noticed (commits and branch switches are instant via a file watcher). Default 4.

server.name: io.github.maxf98/memory
server.title: Memory
server.description: A persistent key-value store for buttons, exposed as a live resource.

io.github.maxf98.streamdeck-mcp/studio.longDescription: A persistent key-value store for buttons — the one thing a face cannot do for itself. A face runs on an opaque origin with no localStorage and no indexedDB, and its local view state dies when the idle window is dismissed, so without a server a button cannot remember anything between presses. Get/set/delete any JSON value, plus increment_value and toggle_value for the two cases buttons actually need (a press counter, a latching toggle). The whole store is also a live resource (resource://memory/store), so a face can bind it and repaint when a value changes.

io.github.maxf98.streamdeck-mcp/studio.longDescription: Structured LLM calls, image analysis (GPT-4o vision), image generation and editing (GPT Image — written to disk and returned as a path, never as inline base64), and Whisper audio transcription. All tools share a single API key.

server.name: io.github.maxf98/photoshop
server.title: Photoshop
server.description: Drive Photoshop by script: layers, selections, filters and generative AI.

io.github.maxf98.streamdeck-mcp/studio.longDescription: Drive Adobe Photoshop by script — 100 tools covering documents, layers (create/order/transform/properties/masks), selections, text, filters, colour adjustments, layer styles, history, actions, data sets, image stacks, export/place, and the generative-AI family (fill, remove, expand, upscale, sky replacement, generate image). Includes 16 multi-step recipe tools that run a whole workflow (remove background, enhance portrait, frequency separation, batch watermark, CSV to cards…) inside one suspended history state, so a single Undo reverts the lot. Works by running ExtendScript inside Photoshop over AppleScript's `do javascript`, with no plugin to install. Also exposes the active document's live state as a subscribable resource (resource://photoshop/document) plus key, dial and popup surfaces.

io.github.maxf98.streamdeck-mcp/studio.longDescription: Search the web and read pages. search_web and search_news query the Brave Search API (needs a free API key); fetch_url retrieves any http(s) page and returns it as readable text, and needs no key at all. fetch_url is also how a face reaches an HTTP API it cannot call itself — a face runs on an opaque origin, so its own fetch is blocked by CORS for most hosts, while a pack request carries no Origin.

server.name: io.github.maxf98/window_management
server.title: Window Management
server.description: Move, resize and snap windows across displays, with windows as live resources.

io.github.maxf98.streamdeck-mcp/studio.longDescription: Move, resize and snap windows across screens; open, close and place windows across displays and spaces. The tools ACT; the observable state is subscribable resources — the app list, the open windows, the displays, the Mission Control spaces and the frontmost app, each with a schema a face can bind to. Windows are addressed by stable handles (get_windows and new_window return one per window) rather than by a z-order index that shifts as windows are focused. Multi-monitor aware: a new window lands on the display the pointer is on rather than wherever the app cascaded it, and any window can be pulled to the display in front of you. Also ships an app-switcher across three Stream Deck surfaces — a key (press cycles apps), a dial (rotate to preview, press to switch), and a popup grid — as live MCP App UI resources with in-component handlers.

server.title: Gmail
server.description: Google's hosted Gmail MCP server: read and compose mail.

notes: accounts.google.com has NO registration_endpoint, so these need a pre-registered Google Cloud OAuth client. It is a public/PKCE desktop client, so there is no secret — the client id gates AVAILABILITY, not confidentiality.

NOT SHIPPABLE YET — do not set GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID in production. These need Google OAuth verification first. Testing mode is not an escape hatch: <=100 listed test users, an unverified-app warning, and consent + refresh tokens expire after 7 days, so buttons would break weekly.
Scope class: RESTRICTED — needs Google verification plus an annual paid CASA security assessment.
Only Gmail is publicly documented; the rest follow the same `<app>mcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1` shape and are live.

headers.name: Authorization
headers.description: GitHub personal access token, sent as `Bearer <token>`.

server.name: io.github.maxf98/slack
server.title: Slack
server.description: Slack's hosted MCP server: search, messages, channels and canvases.

io.github.maxf98.streamdeck-mcp/studio.scopes: search:read.public chat:write channels:history users:read users:read.email canvases:read canvases:write
notes: Pre-registered OAuth app: Slack requires a client SECRET, so the code->token exchange runs on the registry service and `exchangeProxy` tells the Studio to route its redirect through it. The secret stays a Railway env var.

The client id is a literal here because this list is published as a static file. That is not a leak: a client id is public by construction (it rides in every authorize URL) and this exact value has been served unauthenticated from /registry all along.
The scopes are USER scopes (sent as user_scope in the authorize URL) because Slack's MCP server needs a user token (xoxp-), not a bot token (xoxb-).
Note `search:read.public`, not `search:read`: the broader scope needs Slack approval the app does not have.
